## Why

The Go rewrite evaluation (`research/go-rewrite-evaluation.md`, merged 2026-10-15) found two places where the invariant docs that agents read disagree with the code. First, `ARCHITECTURE.md:266-267`, `docs/getting-started.md:911` and the comment at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:34` say `check` "never shells out to git". Since s301, `check.run` calls `_sibling_collisions` (`src/slicer/check.py:61`), which runs `vcs.is_repo`, `vcs.resolve`, `store.sibling_checkouts` and, when titles differ, `verify.inherited_ids` (`src/slicer/check.py:74-85`), all git subprocesses; the collision paragraph in `ARCHITECTURE.md` itself says so, so the document contradicts itself. Second, `ARCHITECTURE.md:195-196` lists `mv` and `ls-files` in `vcs.ALLOWED`, but the allowlist (`src/slicer/vcs.py:17-20`) has neither. Both drifts are in the safe direction, but these paragraphs document the git invariant and must be exact.

- `ARCHITECTURE.md`: the "What `check` is" section says `check` runs read-only git calls only for the sibling-worktree collision warning, skipped outside a repository, and still writes nothing to git; the allowlist sentence names exactly the entries in `vcs.ALLOWED`.
- `docs/getting-started.md` (the CI section near line 911) and the comment in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: a shallow checkout is still fine, because a CI clone has no sibling worktrees; say that instead of "never shells out to git".
